<description>
The first commit of this PR has a minor non breaking API change, it renames the `estimatesmartfee` default estimator option name from "none" to "auto"

----

The mempool fee rate estimator can't always return an estimate:

i)   right after first startup (or after re-syncing through IBD) it hasn't tracked
     enough recent blocks yet;
ii)  the mempool is empty or too sparse to fill the requested block percentile,
     e.g. after a cold restart with persistence off or a missing/corrupt
     mempool.dat.
iii) recent blocks cover too little of the mempool (low coverage); and
iv)  the mempool is still loading.

Previously, case (ii) with a healthy mempool will returned the fee rate
floor (the higher of the minimum relay fee and the current mempool minimum fee).
This can be a significant underestimation, since the now-missing mempool may have
held much higher-feerate transactions. The remaining cases surfaced the mempool
error directly from the combined estimate.

This PR makes the combined estimate (`estimatesmartfee` with
`fee_rate_estimator=none`, the default) fall back to the block policy estimate
whenever the mempool estimator isn't ready, instead of returning the floor or
surfacing the error:

- The mempool estimator now returns an error instead of flooring an unfilled
  percentile, so an empty/sparse mempool is treated like any other not-ready
  state rather than potentially silently underestimating.
- The combined estimate starts from the block policy estimate and only lowers it
  with the mempool estimate when one is available. An error is returned only when
  the block policy estimate itself is unavailable.
- Calling `estimatesmartfee` with `fee_rate_estimator=mempool_policy` explicitly
  still returns the failure.

When the mempool fails to load at startup (persistence off, or a missing/corrupt
mempool.dat), init notifies the estimator, which clears its tracked mined-block
window. Otherwise the estimator would keep a window describing a mempool the node
no longer has; clearing it makes the estimator report insufficient data until the
window refills from the current tip, so the combined estimate falls back to block
policy meanwhile.

This is an alternative to #36095.
</description>

[2026-09-28] c:5868274728 comment by ismaelsadeeq (member):
@davidgumberg raised a concern that, with the last two commits, we may overestimate for everyone when the mempool is empty (see thread: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36182#discussion_r4088236014).

My rationale for including those two commits before 32.0 is that they preserve the status quo: an empty mempool occurs rarely, whereas users restarting after a while and losing their transaction backlog happens more often. However, an empty mempool is also a valid state and with the last two commits when it occur we overestimate for everyone else.

I discussed this offline with @davidgumberg, and we concluded that the core issue is being able to distinguish a genuinely empty mempool from a missing backlog. We decided to move forward with the first three commits and discuss the issue further and also these are very edge cases that may not warrant the energy.

I split the PR and converted this one into a draft. The first three commits are, IMO, what should be in the 32.x milestone.

Thanks for the review and feedback, all.
